pages.text: Mathematics breeds anomalies from perfectly good rules. In 1872 a sum of cosines, W(x) = Σaⁿcos(bⁿπx), turned out to be continuous everywhere and differentiable nowhere: a $(thing)monster$(), as Poincaré called such things. Its graph is a fractal of dimension 2 + ln a/ln b. Then came sets with no measure, space-filling curves, a sphere cut into a few pieces that reassemble into two.

$(thing)Chaos$(): a deterministic system such as the logistic map xₙ₊₁ = rxₙ(1 − xₙ) can amplify every error exponentially - a positive Lyapunov exponent - and settle onto a $(thing)strange attractor$(), a fractal it never leaves and never repeats. Predicted exactly, it cannot be predicted at all.

$(thing)Undecidability$(): some questions have answers no algorithm can find - whether a program halts, whether a statement follows from the axioms. Gödel and Turing showed the anomaly is built in. The $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$() compiles a Gödel sentence, a fractal set and a specimen into $(item)Undecidable Kernels$(): programs no other program can predict.
A program no other program can predict: whether it halts is true or false, and provably unprovable. It runs on anyway.$(br2)Made in $(item)Formal Proof Assistant$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Undecidable Kernel$(): Anomaly Catalogue, Quine Replicator, Resolved Anomaly
